WR_DJ3.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 90 km away; by road, Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri on NH 110. The toy train starts at New Jalpaiguri.

evidence.quote: located 90 km (56 mi) from Darjeeling
Darjeeling can be reached by motorized vehicles on National Highway 110, from Siliguri, 77 km (48 mi) away.

WR_DJ5.claim: October to November offers the clearest mountain views; April to June is also pleasant.

evidence.quote: October to November offers the clearest views
The best time to visit Observatory Hill is from April to June, when the weather is pleasant and clear for panoramic views of the mountains and Darjeeling.

WR_DH2.claim: Built between 1879 and 1881, the 2-ft-gauge line runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling, climbing from about 100 m to 2,200 m with six zig-zags and three loops.

evidence.quote: Built between 1879 and 1881, it is about 88 km (55 mi) long.
It climbs from about 100 m (330 ft) above sea level at New Jalpaiguri to about 2,200 m (7,200 ft) at Darjeeling, using six zig zags and three loops (originally five) to gain altitude.

WR_DH3.claim: Ghum station sits at 2,260 m; at Batasia Loop (1919), 5 km from Darjeeling, the track spirals around a hill beside the Gorkha War Memorial.

evidence.quote: Ghum station is situated at an altitude of 2,260 metres (7,410 ft)
At this point, the track spirals around over itself from the bottom of a small hill and over the hilltop. It was commissioned in 1919.
It is 5 km (3 mi) from Darjeeling, below Ghum

WR_TH2.claim: In peak season crowds and traffic jams are common; Incredible India suggests arriving around 3:30 am.

evidence.quote: in peak season, there is always a throng of people making their way up – and traffic jams are not uncommon. Arrive early, around 3:30 am, to secure a spot.

WR_HV3.claim: Incredible India lists opening hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 04:30 PM

WR_ZO2.claim: Incredible India lists 8:30 am–4:30 pm in summer and 8:30 am–4 pm in winter.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:30 AM to 04:30 PM (Summers)
08:30 AM to 04:00 PM (Winters)

WR_KB2.claim: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport at Dum Dum is about 16 km north-east of the centre.

evidence.quote: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, located in Dum Dum, about 16 km (9.9 mi) north-east of the city centre

WR_KB3.claim: Long-distance trains use Howrah, Sealdah, Kolkata, Shalimar and Santragachi stations; Howrah is India's largest and busiest railway complex.

evidence.quote: Kolkata has five long-distance inter-city railway stations, located at Howrah (the largest and busiest railway complex in India
Sealdah (2nd busiest in India
Kolkata, Shalimar and Santragachi Junction, which connect Kolkata by rail

WR_KB10.claim: Durga Puja, in September–October, is Kolkata's biggest festival.

evidence.quote: Durga Puja, held in September–October, is Kolkata's most important and largest festival

WR_WBF_AIR.claim: Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International is the largest airport; Bagdogra near Siliguri serves the hills.

evidence.quote: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport at Dum Dum, Kolkata, is the state's largest airport.

WR_WBF_WIN.claim: Winter (December–January) is mild on the plains, averaging minimums of about 15 °C; the Darjeeling hills have a harsh winter with occasional snow.

evidence.quote: Winter (December–January) is mild over the plains with average minimum temperatures of 15 °C (59 °F).
The Darjeeling Himalayan hill region experiences a harsh winter, with occasional snowfall.

WR_WBF_MON.claim: The monsoon rains fall from June to September; Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Cooch Behar get over 250 cm.

evidence.quote: Monsoons bring rain to the whole state from June to September.
Heavy rainfall of above 250 centimetres (98 in) is observed in the Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, and Cooch Behar district.

WR_WBF_DURGA.claim: Durga Puja, the state's best-loved festival and a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, falls in Ashvin (September–October).

evidence.quote: West Bengal hosts the world-renowned festival of Durga Puja designated an Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO.
The festival is observed in the Indian calendar in the month of Ashvin (September–October) on the Hindu luni-solar calendar.

WR_KLM1.claim: Kalimpong is a hill station at 1,250 m with the Zang Dhok Palri Phodang monastery and a cactus nursery of over 3,000 varieties.

evidence.quote: Perched at an altitude of 1,250 meters, this beautiful hill station is a great getaway to unwind and relax.
No visit to Kalimpong would be complete without a visit to the renowned Zang Dhok Palri Phodang monastery.
an impressive collection of over 3,000 varieties of cacti and succulents

WR_WBF7.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 75 km away — about 3 hours by taxi or shared vehicle; New Jalpaiguri station is about 72 km, 2–3 hours from Siliguri.

evidence.quote: The nearest major airport to Kalimpong is Bagdogra Airport, which is located approximately 75 km away.
From Bagdogra, you can hire a taxi or take a shared vehicle to Kalimpong, which is about a 3-hour trip.
The nearest major railway station to Kalimpong is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), located around 72 km away.
You can hire a taxi or take a shared vehicle from Siliguri, which will take around 2-3 hours

WR_WBF8.claim: Teesta rafting starts at Teesta Bazaar, 45 km away; March–June and September–November are best.

evidence.quote: The river-rafting center is located at Teesta Bazaar, 45 kilometers from Kalimpong

WR_WBF1.claim: Visitors need permission from the Field Director's office at Canning or at Sonakhali, Bagna, Sajnekhali or Jhingakhali, paying entry fees for the boat and visitors; foreigners need no special permit but must carry their visa and documents.

evidence.quote: Visitors require permission to visit Sundarban Tiger Reserve, which can be obatined from the office of the Field Director, Sundarban Tiger Reserve, Canning 24 Parganas (S), Sonakhali, Bagna, Sajnekhali, Jhingakhali, on payment of entry fee for boat and for visitors.
Foreigners compulsorily require their Visa and necessary documents
No special permits are required for foreigners.

WR_WBF2.claim: Tourists may enter only in registered tourist boats, with a compulsory eco-guide for the whole cruise; inside the reserve, boats and launches are the only transport.

evidence.quote: Any tourist can enter into STR only with the registered tourist boats
Visitors compulsorily require hiring eco-guides, who would escort them during the entire cruise inside the Tiger Reserve.
Within Sundarban, the only way to get around is by boat or launch.

WR_WBF3.claim: Canning is the nearest station, with EMU trains from Sealdah every hour; buses to Sonakhali and Godkhali leave from Esplanade.

evidence.quote: The nearest railhead to Sundarban Tiger Reserve is Canning Railway Station.
Trains (EMU) to reach Canning, are available from Sealdah at an interval of every one hour.

WR_WBF4.claim: Boats board at Godkhali and Dhamakhali; Godkhali jetty has private parking, and WBTDC runs guided tours from Kolkata.

evidence.quote: boat boarding point at Godkhali and Dhamakhali
there is a private parking space at Godkhali Jetty Ghat

WR_WBF10.claim: Santiniketan, part of Bolpur about 152 km north of Kolkata, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.

evidence.quote: approximately 152 km north of Kolkata

WR_WBF11.claim: Bolpur Shantiniketan station has trains from Sealdah and Howrah; WBTC runs AC Volvo buses from Kolkata.

evidence.quote: Bolpur Shantiniketan railway station is well connected with Sealdah Railway Station, Howrah Station

WR_WBF13.claim: The Poush Mela runs three days from 7 Poush; Holi is celebrated as Basanta Utsav to welcome spring.

evidence.quote: The largest and most notable fair is the Poush Mela held at Santiniketan for three days from 7 Poush.

WR_WBF14.claim: The Sonajhuri haat runs every day except Wednesday; Ballabhpur Deer Park is 3 km away.

WR_WBK1.claim: Kurseong, at about 1,483 m, is 32 km from Darjeeling and 34 km from Siliguri, linked by road and the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.

evidence.quote: Located at an altitude of 1,482.55 metres (4,864.0 ft), Kurseong is 32 kilometres (20 mi) from Darjeeling

WR_WBK3.claim: Kurseong is renowned for its tea estates, among them Makaibari, one of the oldest.

WR_WBO1.claim: Lolegaon sits at about 1,675 m, 24 km from Lava; Kafer, 1 km away, has a panoramic view of Kanchenjunga.

itineraries.title: North Bengal hills in 6 days: Kurseong, Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Lava
itineraries.summary: Tea at Kurseong, Darjeeling's Toy Train and Tiger Hill sunrise, Kalimpong's Teesta valley, then the forests of Lava and Kanchenjunga from Lolegaon.
itineraries.seoTitle: Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Lava: 6-Day North Bengal Trip
itineraries.seoDescription: 6 days in the North Bengal hills: Kurseong tea, Darjeeling's Toy Train and Tiger Hill, Kalimpong and the Teesta, Lava and Lolegaon, with distances and hours.

plan.overview: A loop through the Darjeeling and Kalimpong hills from Bagdogra or New Jalpaiguri. Start low and green at Kurseong, ride up to Darjeeling for the Toy Train and the Tiger Hill sunrise, cross to Kalimpong above the Teesta, and finish in the forests of Lava and Lolegaon at the edge of Neora Valley.
plan.season: October–November for the clearest views; April–June is also pleasant.
plan.difficulty: Easy to moderate — winding hill roads
plan.transport: Car with driver; the Toy Train for one stretch.

itineraries.title: The Dooars in 4 days: Gorumara, Jaldapara and Buxa
itineraries.summary: Rhinos and elephants in the forests below the Himalayas — safaris at Gorumara and Jaldapara, then the Jayanti river at Buxa.
itineraries.seoDescription: 4 days in the Dooars: Gorumara safaris from Lataguri, Jaldapara's rhinos and Chilapata forest, then Jayanti in Buxa Tiger Reserve, with distances, hours and closures.

plan.overview: The Dooars are the forested plains where the Himalayas meet North Bengal. This trip moves east from Gorumara, known for rhinos, to Jaldapara — West Bengal's biggest rhino population — and on to the Jayanti river in Buxa Tiger Reserve on the Bhutan border.
plan.season: November to March. Gorumara is closed 16 June–15 September.
plan.transport: Car with driver; park safaris by jeep or elephant.

plan.overview: The Sundarbans, home of the Royal Bengal tiger, is the largest mangrove forest in India — almost 4,000 sq km within the tiger reserve. guides.title: How to reach and get around West Bengal
guides.summary: Kolkata and Bagdogra airports, Howrah and New Jalpaiguri stations, the Toy Train to Darjeeling, and how to get to the hills, the Dooars, the Sundarbans and the coast.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach West Bengal and Get Around
guides.seoDescription: Getting around West Bengal: Kolkata and Bagdogra airports, Howrah and NJP stations, the Toy Train, routes to Darjeeling, Kalimpong, the Dooars, Sundarbans and Digha.

body.intro: West Bengal stretches from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal, and it has two gateways: Kolkata for the south and Bagdogra, near Siliguri, for the hills and the Dooars.

items.title: Kolkata
items.body: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International, about 16 km north-east of the centre, is the state's largest airport. Howrah is India's largest railway complex; Sealdah, Kolkata, Shalimar and Santragachi also serve long-distance trains.

items.title: North Bengal
items.body: Bagdogra serves the hills. New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the most important railway station in Northeast India; Siliguri Junction is in town.

items.title: Durgapur
items.body: Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport is about 70 km from Bolpur and Santiniketan.

items.title: Darjeeling
items.body: 77 km from Siliguri; Bagdogra is about 90 km. The Toy Train runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri.

items.title: Kalimpong
items.body: About 75 km from Bagdogra (about 3 hours) and 72 km from NJP.

items.title: Kurseong
items.body: 34 km from Siliguri, on the Toy Train line.

items.title: Gorumara
items.body: 78 km from Bagdogra, 58 km from NJP.

items.title: Jaldapara and Buxa
items.body: Trains to Hasimara, Alipurduar Junction or New Alipurduar; Buxa via Rajabhatkhawa.

items.title: Sundarbans
items.body: Hourly EMU trains from Sealdah to Canning; buses from Esplanade to Sonakhali and Godkhali. Inside, registered boats only.

items.title: Digha
items.body: About 183–187 km from Kolkata; trains from Howrah to Digha station, and buses from Esplanade.

sections.heading: Cooch Behar and buses
sections.text: New Cooch Behar station is 5 km from Cooch Behar town; Bagdogra is 151 km away. North Bengal State Transport Corporation, headquartered in Cooch Behar, runs regular buses across West Bengal; WBTC runs AC Volvo buses from Kolkata to Santiniketan.

guides.title: Best time to visit West Bengal: hills, plains and festivals
guides.summary: Winter for Kolkata and the plains, October–November for clear Himalayan views, the Dooars' monsoon closures, and the festivals worth timing a trip around.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit West Bengal: Season by Season
guides.seoDescription: When to visit West Bengal: mild plains winters, October–November in Darjeeling, Gorumara's monsoon closure, and Durga Puja, Poush Mela and other festivals.

body.intro: West Bengal has summer, the rains, a short autumn and winter. The plains are best in winter, the hills in autumn and spring, and the Dooars parks close for the monsoon.

items.title: Winter (December–January)
items.body: Mild on the plains, with minimums around 15 °C; Kolkata dips to about 9–11 °C. The Darjeeling hills are harsh, with occasional snow.

items.title: Monsoon (June–September)
items.body: Heavy rain; Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Cooch Behar get over 250 cm.

items.title: Darjeeling
items.body: October–November for the clearest views; April–June is also pleasant.

items.title: Kalimpong
items.body: Teesta rafting is best March–June and September–November.

items.title: Gorumara
items.body: November to March; closed 16 June–15 September.

items.title: Durga Puja
items.body: September–October; a UNESCO-listed festival and Kolkata's biggest.
